small_guidance:
- The conv (128×64×128×128 with 3×3) dominates runtime; tuning the IN+div kernel further has little headroom. If staying small, try BLOCK=4096 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and a single-pass Welford to halve global-load traffic on the (N*C=16384) rows of HW≈15876.
- Switch the activation tensor to channels_last so the conv (cuDNN NHWC) and a per-(N,C) IN reduction both coalesce; pass `memory_format=torch.channels_last` through conv and adapt indexing in the IN kernel.
- Add `@triton.autotune` over BLOCK ∈ {1024,2048,4096}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3} keyed on HW.
large_guidance:
- Replace the `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit gather of the 3×3×64 patch into the K dimension, BLOCK_M/N/K=64/64/32 starting point, channels_last input. The conv is the bottleneck (≥80% of 10.3 ms baseline), so this is where headroom lives.
- Fuse the instance-norm and divide-by directly into the conv kernel's epilogue only if you adopt a two-pass strategy (first pass writes conv output + per-(N,C) partial sums via atomics or a second reduction kernel; second pass applies (x-mean)*rstd/divide_by). Simpler: conv kernel writes Y, then a single fused IN+div kernel (already present) consumes it — keep the IN kernel but feed it from a custom conv.
- Fold `1/divide_by` into the conv weight at init (pure scalar affine on the weight and bias is allowed and not a graph shortcut since the conv still runs); this removes one multiply from the IN epilogue.
